3.t: by the even and the odd,

5.t: is this oath strong enough for a rational person?

6.t: Have you [Prophet] considered how your Lord dealt with [the people] of 'Ad,

7.t: of Iram, [the city] of lofty pillars,

8.t: whose like has never been made in any land,

9.t: and the Thamud, who hewed into the rocks in the valley,

10.t: and the mighty and powerful Pharaoh?

11.t: All of them committed excesses in their lands,

13.t: your Lord let a scourge of punishment loose on them.

15.t: [The nature of] man is that, when his Lord tries him through honour and blessings, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me,’

16.t: but when He tries him through the restriction of his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’

17.t: No indeed! You [people] do not honour orphans,

18.t: you do not urge one another to feed the poor,

20.t: and you love wealth with a passion.

21.t: No indeed! When the earth is pounded to dust, pounded and pounded,

22.t: when your Lord comes with the angels, rank upon rank,

23.t: when Hell is that Day brought near- on that Day man will take heed, but what good will that be to him then?

24.t: He will say, ‘Would that I had provided for this life to come!’

25.t: On that Day, no one will punish as He punishes,

26.t: and no one will bind as He binds.

28.t: return to your Lord well pleased and well pleasing;
